lesson_title: Eye Contact Across a Grandstand: the Trig Secret
hook_text: You look down at your friend on the field. They look up at you. Same angle. Every time. Here's the geometry that proves it.
clip_script: Now climb to the top row of the grandstand and look down at a friend standing on the field. Your eyes start level and rotate DOWN. That amount of turn is the angle of depression — how far down from level. Not from the front wall of the stand, not from your shoes: from LEVEL. And a beautiful secret ties the two together. Your level line at the top of the stand and the flat field below are parallel — level lines never meet. Your line of sight to your friend is one straight line crossing both. The angle you look DOWN at your friend equals the angle your friend looks UP at you. Perfect symmetry — two people making eye contact along one straight line.
visual_style: Side-view animation of a grandstand and field: two glowing parallel level lines, a single line of sight connecting two figures, matching angle arcs pulsing at both ends in the same colour.
pacing: Slow climb up the stand, snap to the level lines appearing, line of sight drawn in one stroke, both angles pulse together on the reveal beat.
